module_description: Module 20 is the newest required module: detecting AI-generated text, images, audio and video (deepfakes) in social streams. It covers statistical and learned detectors, provenance/watermarking standards, human perception limits, and the practical analytics problem of measuring how much of a corpus is synthetic. Students train and evaluate a detector on a public synthetic/real dataset and learn its brittleness.
core_concepts: Limits of detection: false alarms, evasion, model drift
learning_outcomes: C3 Train and evaluate a synthetic-content detector
C4 Explain watermarking and provenance as policy/technical tools
C5 Quantify detection error and its consequences for analysis
methods_models: Detector training (fine-tuned classifiers, perplexity-based detectors, watermark detection), forensic features, ensemble with metadata checks
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy, FPR/FNR, robustness under paraphrase and cross-model tests, human vs machine agreement
pitfalls_limitations: Detectors degrade on paraphrased or unseen-generator content; false accusations against human writers; distribution shift with each new model; heavy class imbalance
tools_stack: transformers, image forensics tooling, ROC analysis, watermark libraries where available
commercial_platforms: Brief mention of commercial brand-safety/deepfake detection vendors
tools_access_cost: Detector APIs priced per call; training a small model is free on free GPU tiers
lab_activities: Train a text detector on a public human/AI corpus and test it on paraphrased text and a different generator
datasets_apis: Public AI-generated text datasets, deepfake image/video datasets
assessment_methods: Lab notebook plus graph figures and a short interpretation; graded on correctness of metrics and defensibility of substantive claims
data_collection_workflow: Build the interaction graph from collected data -> deduplicate accounts and edges -> compute metrics -> cluster communities -> archive graph object and code
textbooks: MDPI 2026 special issue paper on synthetic media (deepfakes and beyond)
AI Tracking Center / NewsGuard AI misinformation tracking reports
key_papers: ACM/Nature 2025-2026 empirical analyses of AI-generated misinformation on X
Scoping reviews of generative AI misinformation (2026)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: synthetic content became an analytics object in its own right; provenance and watermarking entered platform policy, so analytics now includes 'share of synthetic posts' as a metric
industry_relevance: Directly used in short-form content strategy, creator-marketing measurement, and social-commerce analytics teams; the metrics in this module (watch time, completion, saves, CTR via video) are the same KPIs agencies report to clients.
localization_context: Taught against the Indonesian short-video and live-commerce ecosystem (TikTok Shop, live shopping sessions, Shopee/Tokopedia live), which has different content formats and monetization mechanics from the US market.
ethics_regulation: Disclosure of paid partnerships, sponsored content and affiliate links; UU PDP and platform rules on scraping engagement data; caution when profiling creators and audiences from public metrics.
case_study_scenarios: Estimate what share of posts about a local issue are AI-generated and how confident you can be.
deliverable_format: Detector + uncertainty report on a sample corpus
